Taylor expansion with dominated Gaussian integral gives linear Neumann versus cubic Dirichlet scaling. These are analytic proofs, supplemented by 10,053 successful checker assertions.

value.rationale: The result completely identifies what a squared Hilbert–Schmidt boundary-condition comparison can and cannot distinguish: all measurable masks of equal Gaussian mass have the same contrast, and maximal contrast has an exact attained quarter bound. The canonical boundary-attached mask has a unique reflecting-wall overshoot while its absorbing counterpart rises strictly and loses two powers of small-window mass. These are natural structural invariants and a complete geometry-specific classification, rather than a routine normalization check.
